INSTRUCTIONS.TITLE: About Visual Analysis
INSTRUCTIONS.INTRO: This module lets you inspect the invariant-mass results collected by students in a selected session.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_1: Choose a session from the dropdown above the Results table.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_2: The Mass Histograms show the combined distribution of particle masses reported by the selected students.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_3: In the Results table, select or deselect students to include or exclude their data from the histograms.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_4: Use the refresh button if new student results become available.
INSTRUCTIONS.HOW_TO_READ_INTRO: Each histogram shows the invariant mass of a candidate particle:
INSTRUCTIONS.CLEAR_PEAK: A clear peak indicates that students correctly identified that particle.
INSTRUCTIONS.BROAD_DISTRIBUTION: A broad or flat distribution may mean misidentification or too few candidates.
INSTRUCTIONS.TIP: Compare histograms across students or sessions to see how consistently the class reconstructed each particle species.

INSTRUCTIONS.TITLE: About Large Scale Analysis
INSTRUCTIONS.INTRO: This module combines results from a masterclass event to study strangeness enhancement — how the production of strange particles increases in heavy-ion Pb–Pb collisions relative to proton–proton collisions.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_1: Choose an event from the dropdown above the plot.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_2: The plot shows strangeness enhancement as a function of collision centrality, measured by the number of participating nucleons Npart.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_3: The Results table lists yields and enhancement values for each centrality class and particle species.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_4: Use the refresh button if new results become available.
INSTRUCTIONS.YIELD_DEF: efficiency-corrected yield per event: reconstructed particle count divided by (number of analysed events × reconstruction efficiency)
INSTRUCTIONS.NPART_DEF: average number of nucleons participating in the collision
INSTRUCTIONS.ENHANCEMENT_DEF: yield per participant, normalised to a pp reference:
INSTRUCTIONS.WHERE_YPP: where Ypp is the reference yield in pp collisions.
INSTRUCTIONS.FACTOR_TWO: The factor 2 converts the pp yield to a per-participant scale, since a pp collision involves two protons.
